ing: cut into pieces, or chicken thighs
dry, optional; use broth to skip
st: Pat the rabbit dry and season with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the rabbit well in batches, about 10 minutes total. Remove it.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute and the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and scrape the bottom of the pot. Boil for 3 minutes to cook off the alcohol.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth and bay leaves, then return the rabbit to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low for 90 minutes, stirring now and then, until the meat is very tender and nearly falls off the bone.
Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes if using. Taste and adjust the salt.
Sprinkle with parsley. The sauce is often served over spaghetti and the rabbit as a second course.
Mix the flour and [[0.5 tsp]] of the salt in a bowl. Rub in [[0.5 cup]] of the cold butter until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Add the cold water a little at a time to form a firm dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough into a long rectangle. Dot with half of the remaining butter, fold in thirds, and chill for 10 minutes. Repeat with the rest of the butter.
Roll the dough into a rectangle about 1/8 inch thick and cut into 12 squares or circles.
Mix the ricotta, beaten egg, remaining salt and pepper. For peas, mash the peas with the onion powder.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Put about [[2 tbsp]] filling on each piece. Fold and pinch the edges to form a boat shape, then place on a lined tray.
Brush with the egg yolk and the melted butter.
Bake for 25 minutes until deep golden and flaky. Serve warm.
Mix the flour, yeast and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and [[1 tbsp]] of the oil and stir to a shaggy dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and springy.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 60 minutes until doubled.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking sheet inside.
Divide the dough in two. Stretch each piece into a flat ring about 8 inches wide by pressing a hole through the center, like a thick donut.
Cut each ring open horizontally and layer with half of the tomatoes, tuna, olives, capers, potatoes and basil on the bottom half.
Close and brush the top with [[1 tbsp]] oil. Slide onto the hot baking sheet.
Bake for 18 minutes until golden. Drizzle with the remaining oil and serve warm.

ing: thick, such as ftira or sourdough
st: Toast the bread slices lightly on both sides.
Cut the tomatoes in half and rub the cut side firmly over each toast so the juice and pulp soak in.
Spread a thin layer of tomato paste over the bread if you want more flavor.
Drizzle each slice with the olive oil.
Flake the tuna onto the bread and add the capers and olives.
Sprinkle with the mint, salt and pepper.
Serve right away, open or pressed into a sandwich.
Rub the butter into the flour and [[0.5 tsp]] of the salt until crumbly. Add cold water to form a dough, wrap, and chill 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato paste and tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, olives, capers, raisins, remaining salt and pepper and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, about 2 minutes. Add the fish and cook gently for 3 minutes. Let the filling cool for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Roll out two-thirds of the dough and line a 9-inch pie dish. Add the filling.
Roll the rest of the dough for a lid, seal the edges, and cut small steam vents. Brush with the egg.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden and the fish reads at least 145°F (63°C). Rest 10 minutes and serve.

ing: cubed, plus extra for the dish
st: Rub the butter into the flour and [[0.5 tsp]] of the salt, add cold water to make a dough, wrap, and chill 30 minutes.
Heat the oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and beef and cook for 8 minutes until browned.
Add the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, remaining salt and pepper. Simmer 20 minutes into a thick sauce.
Cook the pasta 2 minutes short of the package time, drain, and mix with the sauce, [[3 eggs]] beaten, and the cheese.
Fold in the chopped boiled egg if using. Cool 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a deep 9-inch baking dish.
Roll two-thirds of the dough and line the dish with some hanging over. Fill with the pasta.
Roll the rest for a lid, seal the edges, brush with the last beaten egg, and cut a steam hole.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden. Rest 15 minutes, then slice.

ing: with bones, such as snapper, cut in pieces
st: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and gently cook the garlic for 2 minutes, without browning it.
Add the tomato paste and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the water, add the fish, salt, pepper and marjoram, and bring to a boil. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Lift out the fish and set it aside. Strain the broth back into the pot, pressing the tomatoes and garlic through.
Bring the broth back to a boil, add the rice, and cook for 15 minutes until soft.
Remove skin and bones from the fish and return the flesh to the soup.
Stir in the mint and lemon juice. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve hot with crusty bread.
Drain the soaked beans and rinse them well.
Place them in a pot with the water. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Cover and simmer on low for 90 minutes until completely soft, adding hot water if they begin to dry.
Drain, keeping about [[0.5 cup]] of the cooking liquid.
Mash the beans with a fork or masher until thick but not totally smooth.
Mix in the garlic, chili, parsley, olive oil, salt and lemon juice. Add some cooking liquid for a creamy texture.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve at room temperature with crackers or bread.
Simmer the dates with the water, orange zest, orange juice, anise and cinnamon for 10 minutes, mashing until a thick paste forms. Cool for 20 minutes.
Rub the butter into the flour and salt, then add the cold water to make a smooth dough.
Wrap and rest the dough for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough out into a rectangle about 1/8 inch thick and cut into long strips about 4 inches wide.
Spoon a line of date paste down the center of each strip.
Fold the dough over the filling and press to seal, then cut into diamond shapes.
Heat the oil in a pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches for 3 minutes, turning once, until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Serve warm, dusted with powdered sugar.
Drain the ricotta in a sieve in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Mix the flour, dough sugar, salt and butter, then add the wine or vinegar to form a stiff dough. Knead 5 minutes, wrap, and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin, about 1/16 inch, and cut into 4-inch circles.
Wrap each circle around a metal cannoli tube. Seal the edge with beaten egg.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the shells, 2 or 3 at a time, for 2 minutes until golden and blistered. Drain on paper towels and cool, then slip out the tubes.
Beat the drained ricotta with the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth. Stir in the chocolate chips.
Pipe or spoon the filling into the shells just before serving, so they stay crisp.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve.
